prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / detailed painted game sprite movement sheet.
Asset: exactly FOUR full-body rolling keys of ONE robot, in a strict 2 columns x 2 rows layout, on a 1536x1536 transparent RGBA square canvas. Read top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. Each equal square cell is a complete cutout with generous clear alpha margins on every side. This is a travel cycle, not a character design variation or work sequence.
Reference image 1 is the selected detailed FRONT-RIGHT movement sheet. Repaint these same four keys as the new physical direction below; preserve its precise identity, proportions, parts, and wheel phases. Do NOT horizontally flip it. Reference image 2 supplies the elevated game camera only. Reference image 2 supplies ONLY the game's elevated orthographic character-camera angle, not its humanoid anatomy or gait.
CAMERA: fixed orthographic, looking down about 31 degrees, three-quarter diagonal view, 45-degree ground heading. Show tops of cap/body/wheels clearly, as this will be seen in an isometric game from above. No vanishing point, lens perspective, head-on view or low eye-level toy photograph. Same camera, scale and silhouette in all four cells.
MOTION: four restrained rolling keys. Main wheel hubs have one unobtrusive brass index/spoke progressing through quarter-turn phases 12, 3, 6, 9 o'clock in order. Tyres stay circular in 3D projection with consistent axles, width and tread. Both main wheel axles remain fixed relative to the body. Wheel contact baseline is the same within every cell. Body stays almost stable, only 1–2 pixels of suspension settle and a tiny tool/arm response; it does not hop, stride, stretch or change proportions. Preserve all parts and hand grips across keys. No new action, prop, open panel or change of design between frames.
STYLE: high-detail painted game art, warm dark-brown clean outer outlines, fine painterly surface shading, readable cream enamel and deep muted teal, restrained brass with soft wear at handled edges, black rubber tread, amber light. Coherent screw heads, seams, rim thickness and joints with actual connections. Detail should survive downsampling rather than becoming random engravings. Soft warm light from upper left, restrained edge highlights, no ground shadow or floor.
FRAMING: all four robots fully visible, including cap finial, pole lantern if present, wheels and any rear caster. Never cut a silhouette at a cell boundary. Consistent apparent size in all cells; leave at least 8% clear alpha around each robot. No scenery, text, grid, labels, platform, pedestal or background. Actual transparent background, no painted paper/checkerboard or colored rectangle. Do not include other robots or people.
WICK: preserve the approved slim cream-enamel lamplighter. Teal pagoda-brim lantern head, small round brass top finial; a SINGLE round amber spark-face with two warm simple oval eyes on the FRONT only. A narrow cream torso with a small riveted brass service plate mounts directly into a stable cream/teal motor chassis. Two broad rubber DRIVE WHEELS, one on each side of a single axle, plus a small FRONT guide caster. No legs, ankles or shoes. Teal mitten hands on short brass-jointed arms. His near hand firmly grips the same TELESCOPING BRASS LAMP POLE, STOWED UPRIGHT CLOSE TO HIS SIDE for travel; the pole carries a small teal-roofed glazed amber lantern. The pole, hinges, grip, lantern roof, glass frame and hanging connection must remain identical and visibly attached in every cell. The free arm rests naturally at his side. Keep his tall slim silhouette and genuine wheel support; do not turn him into a human or a second street lamp.
HANDEDNESS LOCK: the lamp pole is held by Wick's OWN LEFT HAND in every view and every frame. It is secured beside his OWN LEFT flank, with the same short brass clamp at the left side of his chassis. The right arm is free. Never exchange the grip between hands, duplicate the pole or mirror the chassis fittings.
DIRECTION AND PHYSICAL SIDE VISIBILITY:
FRONT-LEFT / SOUTHWEST, the face points diagonally to the LOWER-LEFT. Wick's OWN LEFT FLANK is now the NEAR visible flank. His LEFT HAND continues to hold the lamp pole on the VIEWER-RIGHT side of his body, now clearly in front of the torso edge. The free RIGHT arm appears on viewer-left and partly farther away. The pole MUST NOT move to viewer-left merely because he faces left. This is the critical handedness difference from a mirror.
Keep the same stowed upright lamp pole, lantern glass, brass hook/hinges and anatomical LEFT hand in all four cells. The little guide caster is on the FRONT of the wheelbase, so it may be partly occluded in rear views; do not relocate it to the back. Match the chosen front sheet's high detail and apparent full-body height.
